Miranda: So, Rocco. What were your impressions of Ferdinand?
Rocco: He's a likeable young man and should be easy to work with. He was honest about his experience, including where he didn't have any.
Miranda: And that would be ...
Rocco: Finances. As we had sensed from the beginning, his experience with public and press relations is impressive. I feel like he'll be a valuable team player.
Miranda: I value your assessment, Rocco. If you say you can work with him, I have full confidence.

Rocco: How do you foresee the nature of our relationship?
Miranda: I would advise you take on a mentoring relationship. Would you mind providing him some guidance?
Rocco: Certainly. But I would suggest asking Janet to establish the nature of our working relationship.
Miranda: Certainly. Do you imagine he might question your leadership?

Rocco: On the contrary. He was quite respectful.
Miranda: I'm glad. Do you have any other thoughts?
Rocco: We must keep in mind that he has exceptional experience with the South American market. My advice to you and everyone is to withhold judgment if his ideas seem a little unreasonable when we think of our local situation. He strikes me as being very intuitive.
Miranda: Thank you Rocco. I'll pass your recommendations on to Janet.

In the workplace, you will often be requested to give, ask for, and respond to advice.

• You can use a conditional sentence (If clause) to give advice.
    If you tell me you can work together, then I have full confidence.

  • Use the verb advise and the pattern advise + someone + to + do something or advise + something.
    I would advise you to take a different approach.
    I would advise a mentoring relationship.

  • Use the advice.
    My advice is to avoid being judgmental.

  • Use the verb suggest and the pattern suggest + doing something.
    I would suggest talking to Marie about that issue.

  • Use must +verb to make a strong recommendation.
    You must keep in mind that he does have a lot of experience.

NOTE: The word advice is a noun and it is uncountable; therefore:
  • it is never used in the plural: advices
  • it never comes after an or a number: an advice
    She gave me a good advice.
    She gave me good advice.

In the workplace, you will be dealing with people from different countries and backgrounds. Therefore, it is important to describe and talk about your feelings and impressions of co-workers. Here is some language you can use to talk about feelings and emotions:

When asking about someone's feelings and impressions of someone you can say:
  • What are your impressions of … (+ someone)?
  • How do you feel about … (+ someone)?
  • Do you have any thoughts on … (+ someone)?

When describing your feelings and impressions of someone you can say:
  • He/She is/was … (+ adjective)
  • As we/I had sensed from the beginning … (+ clause)
  • I feel like … (+ clause)
  • He was quite/very/rather … (+ adjective)
  • He/She strikes me as being … (+ adjective)
James: How do you feel about Danny?
Seth: He strikes me as being very competent.
James: And what are your thoughts on Jane?
Seth: I've had a sense from the beginning that she's very inexperienced.
someone who works well within a team or group
Example: I think he'll be a valuable team player.
These are words you hear when people are working together.
an evaluation of someone or something's qualities or abilities
Example: I value your assessment, Rocco.
to be aware of or imagine something before it happens
Example: How do you foresee the nature of our relationship?
to wait before making a judgment or evaluation about someone until knowing more
Example: I would withhold judgment until you see how his ideas turn out.
the position of being leader or in charge of a group
Example: Do you think he might question your leadership?
a connection between two people where one is responsible for giving training and advice to the other
Example: I would advise a mentoring relationship.
a suggestion or piece of advice
Example: I'll pass your recommendations on to Janet.
On a piece of paper, write down the name of three to five people you work or go to school with.
Write down your feelings and impressions of them. Your partner will do the same.
With your partner, ask and answer questions about your co-workers or classmates.
When appropriate, give your partner advice on how to deal or work with them.
When you are finished, choose the best piece of advice from your partner and vice-versa.

I express my feelings and impressions of my co-workers or classmates.
I ask questions and give advice about my co-workers or classmates.
